newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-New Tenet to take regional focus.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-New Tenet to take regional focus.

text.p: The hospital management company formed in the proposed merger of Tenet HealthCare Corp and OrNda HealthCorp will focus on regional markets, rather than on trying to become a national powerhouse, its chief executive said on Thursday.

Industry analysts expect the company to be the dominant player in southern California and a strong number two in other key markets, including southern Florida, behind industry leader Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp.

"We're very focused ... in a handful of markets where we want to be number one or number two," Jeffrey Barbakow, Tenet's chairman and chief executive officer, said in an interview. "We are not a national powerhouse."
He listed regions where the company will be focused as southern California, southern Florida, parts of Texas, Louisiana and Alabama.
The merged company, with revenues of about $8.5 billion, will still be far from the size Columbia/HCA, which analysts expect to post revenues of about $20 billion in 1996.
In Southern California, the deal boosts Tenet's holdings to 29 hospitals from 13. Pending deals by OrNda will lift the number to 31.
The merging companies said they expected the deal to result in about $70 million in annual cost savings.
Barbakow, who will continue as chairman and chief executive officer of the combined company, said about $15 million will come from interest reductions and the remainder from other cost savings.
He said there would be job cuts from the current combined workforce of 100,000. He declined to give a precise number, but said job cuts would be a "very minor" percentage of the current total.
Tenet's shares ended off 7/8 at 21-1/4, while OrNda added 1/4 to 27-1/2.
Barbakow attributed Tenet's share drop to moves by stock arbitragers.
But analysts said there appeared to be disappointment from some players on Wall Street that Tenet did not do a deal with Columbia/HCA.
"To the extent that there was speculation in Tenet that Columbia might bid for it, we got a little bit of a short-term dislocation," Bear Stearns analyst A.J. Rice said.
